sections.html:
Arkansas County sits in the Delta in the eastern half of the state, on flat farmland laced with bayous. It has two county seats: Stuttgart for the northern district and DeWitt for the southern. DeWitt replaced Arkansas Post as the seat on February 19, 1853, and Stuttgart became a dual seat in the 1920s.

The split has everyday consequences for owners. The assessor and the collector each keep an office in both towns, so a seller in the north can handle paperwork in Stuttgart and a seller in the south can use DeWitt. Rice is the main crop, and the county sits in the largest rice-growing region in the country, so many sales here involve farmland or houses on large lots.

Residents numbered 17,149 in 2020, a drop from 19,019 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 15,836. Stuttgart fell from 9,326 to 8,264 over the decade, and DeWitt from 3,292 to 3,056. The county has about 8,752 housing units and 6,705 households. The owner-occupied rate is 64.6 percent, median value of owner-occupied homes is $138,100, and median gross rent is $843.

Those numbers cover the whole county. A farmhouse outside Almyra or Humphrey and a house inside Stuttgart can differ a great deal, so treat the median as background and not a price for any one property.

Two elected offices split the work. The assessor values the property. The collector bills and receives the payment. Each has an office in DeWitt and one in Stuttgart.

OfficeDeWittStuttgart
Assessor, 870-659-2105101 Court Square, DeWitt, AR 72042312 S. College, Stuttgart, AR 72160
Collector, 870-659-2104101 Court Square, DeWitt, AR 72042302 South College St., Stuttgart, AR 72160

The general county line is 870-659-2099. An online payment site is available at taxpayment.countyservice.net. Confirm contact details with the county before mailing a check.

Under Ark. Code 26-36-201 the collector accepts real estate tax beginning the first business day of March. The last day is October 15, and when that date falls on a weekend or postal holiday you get the following business day. You may pay in pieces until then. Whatever is still open after October 15 is delinquent and picks up a 10% penalty.

  • First business day of March: collector can take payment.
  • Third Monday in August: last day to schedule a hearing with the county board of equalization.
  • October 15: payment deadline.
  • After October 15: delinquent, with a 10% penalty.

Selling the house resets nothing. Tax stays attached to the parcel, so a September closing with the year's bill unpaid means the collector's balance gets settled through the closing.

Market value is the standard. The assessor revisits each property on a cycle of three, four or five years and may compare sales, estimate cost or look at income. If the record shows the wrong square footage or room count, a phone call to the assessor frequently fixes it with no formal appeal.

Still unhappy? Book a hearing before the county board of equalization no later than the third Monday in August. Should the board rule against you, County Court is the next step, then Circuit Court.

sections.h2: Caps, freezes and the homestead credit
sections.html:
Amendment 79 puts ceilings on growth that a buyer will care about. A primary residence's taxable value can climb no more than 5% a year after reappraisal, while other real estate can climb 10%. An owner who is 65 or older, or disabled, has a primary residence whose taxable value cannot rise from reappraisal at all. The homestead credit, up to $600, has to be claimed at the assessor's office.

Benefits like these do not automatically pass to a buyer, whose own bill can differ from yours until they apply. Say so if a buyer is comparing monthly costs.

A tax bill that fell behind is a problem you can solve at the closing table, not a barrier. Ask the collector for the balance due, including any 10% penalty, and have the title company pay it from your proceeds at closing. If the bill was sent to an old address or a deceased parent's name, tell the collector who now owns the property so the next notice reaches the right person.

Bring the deed or a recent statement and photo ID to the closing. Heirs should also bring papers showing who may sign. If the title company asks for anything else, get the request in writing so nothing is missed on closing day.

A modest estate may qualify for the small estate procedure. Ark. Code 28-41-101 caps it at $100,000 and requires a 45-day wait plus a published notice to creditors when real property is involved.

A tenant-occupied house follows the state's landlord-tenant rules. A landlord may end an oral lease with one rental period's notice, or as the written lease provides.

Expect a state transfer tax at closing: $3.30 for each $1,000 of consideration, plus $2.20 per $1,000 that the statute assigns to the purchaser.

Start by picking a route: a listing with an agent, or a direct offer from a cash buyer. Next, call the collector for the current balance and the assessor to confirm how the property is described. Once you accept an offer, a title company searches the record, finds any unpaid tax or lien, and sets a signing date. At the table you sign the deed, the tax is paid from your proceeds and you receive the remainder.

A cash buyer skips the lender, so there is no appraisal wait and no loan to fall through. That helps with farmhouses that need repairs, rentals with a tenant in place, and inherited houses where several family members have to agree.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html: Put together the deed, your latest tax statement, the names of everyone on the title and any receipts for repairs or additions. If the property is farmland or a large lot, find the survey and note any easements or leases, since a farm tenant or hunting lease can affect what a buyer can do with the land. Owners over 65 or disabled should bring proof of any freeze, and anyone who claimed the homestead credit should say so, because the new owner will have to apply on their own.

U.S. Highway 165 links DeWitt and Stuttgart with Little Rock, and Highway 130 runs between the two seats through Almyra. Buyers often look for hunting, wildlife areas and farmland, including the Dale Bumpers White River National Wildlife Refuge and the Bayou Meto Wildlife Management Area, so mention nearby land in a listing. Photos of drainage, ditches and field edges help a buyer judge farmland.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Arkansas County?
faqs.a: The county collector, at 101 Court Square in DeWitt or 302 South College St. in Stuttgart. The phone is 870-659-2104.

faqs.q: When are Arkansas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: From the first business day of March through October 15. Taxes unpaid after October 15 are delinquent and carry a 10% penalty.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal my Arkansas County assessment?
faqs.a: Start with the assessor, who can correct simple errors. For a value dispute, schedule a county board of equalization hearing by the third Monday in August.

faqs.q: Which city is the county seat of Arkansas County?
faqs.a: There are two. Stuttgart serves the northern district and DeWitt serves the southern district.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house if property taxes are still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax follows the parcel, so ask the collector for the balance due and arrange for it to be paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
